newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Virgin to withdraw from Sun Air bidding.
newsitem.headline: Virgin to withdraw from Sun Air bidding.

text.p: Virgin Atlantic said on Friday it intended to withdraw from the bidding process for the privatisation of domestic South African carrier Sun Air.

Virgin Atlantic Bhekilanga Consortium's non-binding bid submitted earlier this month was one of four bids accepted by the South African Ministry of Transport for the sale of 100 percent of the airline.
Other bids were submitted by Malaysia Airlines Consortium, Comair Consortium and Phoenix Venture Partners Consortium.
Virgin said it had decided to withdraw its bid in order to pursue an alternative course of investment in the development of Virgin Atlantic's Southern Africa operation.

"Virgin Atlantic will, however, maintain its commercial relationship with Sun Air and will continue its codeshare arrangement, on services between Johannesburg and Durban and Johannesburg and Cape Town," it said in a statement.
The sale of Sun Air -- South Africa's first full privatisation -- is expected to be concluded by August, after final binding bids are submitted by the remaining bidders by July 21.
Industry analysts have speculated that the sale of Sun Air could fetch around 100 million rand. The airline operates eight aircraft on routes between Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban.
